evidence.note: Lopes and Cornelli explicitly place Letter VI among the letters they regard as spurious.
The review of Morrow reports that he was strongly inclined to recognize Letter VI as authentic.
Helfer (2023) offers a recent scholarly defense of a unified Platonic authorship/design for the Letters.

rationale: Letter VI is one of the minor letters with a substantial defense tradition. Morrow was inclined to accept it and twentieth-century scholarship repeatedly treated it as authentic or at least close to Plato, while Lopes and Cornelli reject it together with the other minor letters. Because the competing positions are serious and persistent, B is preferable to a one-sided C.
